t:
(a) Submission of Plan to Congress.—Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration, in consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Secretary of Defense, shall submit to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Homeland Security of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate a plan for the D.C. Metropolitan Area Special Flight Rules Area. 
    (b) Contents of Plan.—The plan shall outline specific changes to the D.C. Metropolitan Area Special Flight Rules Area that will decrease operational impacts and improve general aviation access to airports in the National Capital Region that are currently impacted by the zone.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "in consultation with" and the submission of a plan signal participation. But the consultation is only between federal officials (the FAA Administrator and the Secretaries of Homeland Security and Defense), and the plan goes to congressional committees, all of which are inside the federal government. No state, local, industry, expert, or public party is brought into the decision, even though the plan aims to benefit general aviation.
fable.s: the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration, in consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Secretary of Defense, shall submit to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure

opus.w: The only consultation is between the FAA Administrator and the Secretaries of Homeland Security and Defense, which is coordination between federal agencies. The plan goes to congressional committees, which are also inside the federal government. The word "consultation" and the goal of improving general aviation access may suggest outside input, but no non-federal party is brought into the decision.
opus.s: the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration, in consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Secretary of Defense, shall submit to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Homeland Security of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate a plan
opus.b:
I labelled this **No**: everyone involved is part of the federal government.

**Why "Yes" is tempting:** the section uses the word "consultation," requires a plan, and talks about improving general aviation access. That could make it look like outside users have a say.

**Why that reading fails:** every actor named is inside the federal government.
- The FAA Administrator consults only with the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Secretary of Defense, which is coordination between federal agencies.
- The plan goes to committees of the House and Senate, and Congress is inside the federal government.
- No states, local governments, airport operators, pilot groups or members of the public are consulted. There is no hearing, comment period, advisory panel or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the FAA Administrator to consult with other federal cabinet secretaries (Homeland Security and Defense) and submit a plan to congressional committees. All actors involved (FAA, DHS, DoD, Congress) are inside the federal government. The definition explicitly excludes intra-governmental coordination and reports to Congress from being considered participation. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with any outside entities such as states, tribes, the public, or private organizations.
qwen_chat.s: the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration, in consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Secretary of Defense, shall submit to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Homeland Security of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate a plan
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Secretary of Defense" constitutes participation because it involves coordination before a decision (submitting the plan). However, both the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Secretary of Defense are federal officials inside the executive branch. The definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination *between* federal agencies or federal officials is not participation. Furthermore, the plan is submitted *to* Congress, which is also inside the federal government. There is no involvement of outside parties (states, tribes, public, experts, etc.) in the decision-making process described in this section.
